display.purpose: The status line only: whose move, who won, or a draw.

title.purpose: The Score heading on the pad and the New Game label.

score-label.purpose: Blue, Red and Draws row labels on the pad.

body.purpose: The hint under the status line from 640px up.

body-sm.purpose: The hint below 640px; the credit line at 1024px and up.

shadows.name: pad-on-desk
shadows.purpose: The legal-pad score sheet lying on the desk.

shadows.name: block-rest
shadows.purpose: Beech block at rest: sanded bevel plus cast depth.

shadows.name: block-pressed
shadows.purpose: Beech block pressed 3px into the desk.

shadows.name: fallback-board
shadows.purpose: Flat beech board shown without WebGL.

motion.name: block-press
motion.purpose: Transform and shadow on the beech block; filter uses 160ms ease-out. Removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: block-press-travel
motion.purpose: How far the beech block sinks when pressed.

motion.name: block-hover
motion.purpose: The only hover response on the beech block.

motion.name: piece-drop
motion.value: start +2.4 units, gravity 22, restitution 0.32, settle below |v| 0.6, step cap 1/30s
motion.purpose: Simulated fall and damped bounce of every newly placed piece.

motion.name: piece-tilt-settle
motion.purpose: The piece lands slightly tipped and rights itself.

motion.name: piece-yaw-jitter
motion.purpose: Deterministic per-cell rotation so a full board looks hand-placed.

motion.name: win-hop-spin
motion.value: 0.9s; lift sin(pi*p)*0.55 + 0.12 hold; spin 2*pi on ease-out cubic; emissive 0.18
motion.purpose: Winning three rise, turn once and glow after settling.

motion.name: win-strike
motion.value: progress rate 1/0.55s, starts at 0.35 of progress (~0.19s), done at ~0.55s, ease-out cubic
motion.purpose: Lacquered bar painted from the first winning square to the third.

motion.name: ease-out-cubic
motion.purpose: Easing for the win spin and win strike.

motion.name: camera-lean
motion.value: pointer x * 0.35, pointer y * 0.2, smoothing 1 - exp(-2.5 * dt)
motion.purpose: Camera drifts toward the pointer like leaning over the table. Fixed under reduced motion.

motion.name: ghost-preview
motion.value: opacity 0.38, no shadow, no depth write, no drop
motion.purpose: Translucent next-player piece over the hovered or focused empty square.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Pieces appear at rest, winners lift to 0.12 without arc or spin, strike drawn complete, camera fixed, block transition none.

components.name: New Game Block

narrative.overview:
The whole page is one physical scene: a sanded beech Tic-Tac-Toe board with carved dark grooves, lying on a walnut desk in warm daylight, with chunky lacquered pieces in toy primaries. The board is the interface. Players touch a square on the 3D board, a translucent ghost of their piece previews the move, and the piece falls, bounces and settles under simulated gravity. Everything else on the page is another object on the same desk: a sheet torn from a canary legal pad that keeps score in ballpoint tally marks, and a beech block cut from the same wood as the board that says New Game.

Density is low and the hierarchy is blunt. One very large status line in chalk white tells you whose move it is, who won, or that it is a draw, with a small drawing of the piece in front of it. A quiet hint sits under it. Nothing else competes. Personality comes from materials (grain, lacquer, paper, ink) and from motion that only happens because a player did something. The world rejects the category default of a flat 3x3 grid of buttons in a centred card; the flat grid exists only as the no-WebGL fallback, and even there it is cut from beech.

The DOM layer and the 3D layer share one palette (`palette.ts` mirrored by the CSS custom properties), so an SVG piece in the status line and a lacquered piece on the board read as the same object.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed 3D walnut desk; the beech board is framed into whatever space the overlay leaves free.
Two player colours only: cobalt for Blue X, vermilion for Red O.
One typeface, Bricolage Grotesque, carrying hierarchy through weight and size.
Physical objects instead of cards: paper sheet, wood block, carved board.
Motion is physics and is always caused by play: drop, damped settle, winning hop and spin, a painted strike.
Reduced motion shows every end state instantly; nothing is lost but the travel.

rules.name: The Two Primaries Rule
rules.body: Cobalt means Blue X and vermilion means Red O, everywhere and only. A control, a heading or a border never borrows a player colour.

rules.name: The One Palette Rule
rules.body: A colour that exists in both the scene and the DOM is the same hex in both. The SVG piece icons import the scene palette directly; the CSS custom properties repeat it by hand.

rules.name: The Chalk On Walnut Rule
rules.body: Text that floats on the desk is chalk (primary) or chalk dim (secondary). Text on the pad is ink. Text on wood is groove.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is the only face. Hierarchy comes from weight (800 / 700 / 600 / 500 / 400) and size, not from a second family.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Score numbers always use tabular figures so a count changing from 9 to 10 never shifts its neighbours.

rules.name: The Objects Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Every raised DOM element is a named desk object (paper, wood block, board) with the material to match, never a generic panel.

rules.name: The Still At Rest Rule
rules.body: At rest, shadows and positions never change. Depth changes only in response to a press.

dos: Do take every colour from the frontmatter; when a colour exists in both the scene and the DOM, use the same hex in both.
Do keep cobalt for Blue X and vermilion for Red O and nothing else.
Do make each raised element a desk object with its material: canary paper with rules (2.5rem) and a margin, beech blocks with the bevel shadow, carved wood.
Do cast DOM shadows as warm, long, soft drops with negative spread (rgba of dark brown or near-black), as in the shadow vocabulary.
Do set every text in Bricolage Grotesque; give counts tabular figures.
Do tie every animation to a player action, simulate the drop rather than tweening it, and show the end state instantly under reduced motion.
Do keep the board itself as the control, with real focusable buttons behind it and a spoken description of every move.
donts: Don't present the board as a flat 3x3 grid of buttons in a centred card; the flat grid is only the no-WebGL fallback.
Don't use a player colour for controls, headings, borders or text.
Don't use grey or cool shadows, or lift objects on hover.
Don't add idle or ambient motion (floating pieces, looping glows, auto-rotating board).
